# `silk/platform/windows/time_zone`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The time zone setting of Windows.

## When to use
The `OsLocalZone` provider of `silk.time.zones_native` uses [`WindowsTimeZone`](#WindowsTimeZone) on Windows.
Application code requires the `LocalZone` effect of `silk.time.zones` and does not call this
module.

## Details
Windows names its zones with its own names, such as `E. South America Standard Time`, and
ships no IANA zone files. [`WindowsTimeZone.keyName`](#WindowsTimeZone.impl.keyName) reads the name of the zone that the
machine is set to, and the provider maps it to an IANA name with the table of the Unicode
CLDR project in the time zone bundle of the standard library.

Import as `WindowsTimeZone` with `import silk.platform.windows.time_zone { WindowsTimeZone }`.

<a id="WindowsTimeZone.impl.keyName"></a>

### Associated function `keyName`

```silk
pub effect fn keyName() -> Option<Bytes> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the Windows name of the zone that the machine is set to, such as
`E. South America Standard Time`, or `None` if Windows does not answer or the name is
empty or not ASCII.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the name.
